revision_note: Revision 2 (C0-POR1-R1). Revision 1 carried provenance labels it had not earned ('vanilla', 'modified'), two wrong totals, and several over-scoped interpretations. This revision replaces them. Counts are NO LONGER restated here: they are generated into c0-por1-census.json by por1_census.py, so there is one source for them rather than two that can diverge. This file carries provenance, qualitative findings and their scope limits.

companion_files.docs/receipts/data/c0-por1-census.json: Generated. Exact reconciled counts by root, folder, extension, subfolder, group and observed structural tuple.
companion_files.docs/receipts/data/c0-por1-specimen-hash: Generated. Exact specimen paths, SHA-256 digests and the full PS3/Xbox 360 comparison output.
companion_files.docs/receipts/data/c0-por1-tools/: The inspection parsers, census and specimen tools, with a README giving invocation and hashes.
companion_files.docs/receipts/c0-por1-portrait-measureme: The original measurement record, with an appended corrections log.
The correction record. Governs wherever the two differ.

preservation.method: SHA-256 computed at first read of each named specimen and recomputed after all inspection completed.
preservation.scope: 22 named specimens only. This says NOTHING about the other 47 520 inventoried files, which were opened read-only but were not hashed before and after. No claim of whole-corpus preservation is made.
preservation.access_mode: every open was read-binary; no write, repack, replace, install or runtime launch occurred at any source location

vocabulary.note: Revision 1 used 'vanilla' and 'modified'. Neither was established, so both are withdrawn. Groups are named by what was actually observed.
vocabulary.current: a file whose extension is .big or .gnf
vocabulary.backup-labelled: a file whose extension is .bak. The label is the filename's; nothing here establishes who wrote it, when, or that its content is original.
vocabulary.other: a file that is neither, i.e. the one .options build artefact
vocabulary.base-level-only header: a texture header whose mip count is 0 and whose payload is exactly one level
vocabulary.mip-chain header: a texture header declaring more than one level
vocabulary.withdrawn: Neither a .bak sibling nor mipMapCount = 0 establishes that a file is EA-authored or unmodified.

evidence_levels.inspected-corpus-invariant: holds for every file inspected in that root, across ALL groups. A property that holds only within a group defined by that property is not an invariant - it is circular.
evidence_levels.target-requirement: what the shipped title requires. NOTHING in this package reaches this level: no load test, no acceptance test and no shipping-manifest check was performed on any target.

locations.tree_kind_evidence: RPCS3 dev_hdd0/game install; the portraits are loose files in the title's own directory layout. The only archives at USRDIR root are options.viv and patch.big.
tree_kind_limits: NOT established to be a pristine shipping layout. No shipping manifest was checked.
patch.big is present at USRDIR root and was NEVER OPENED. It could shadow or supersede loose files; nothing here rules that out.
The copy carries third-party writes: 206 backup-labelled files and 206 current files with mip-chain headers where the remainder have base-level-only headers.

folder_spelling_discrepancy.note: Neither requested spelling exists. The difference is a missing plural 's', not a backslash-escape artefact - the supplied paths contained no backslash before an underscore. The three supplied roots verified exactly as written. The real directory names are used throughout and no other directory was substituted.

build_toolchain_artifact.significance: A leftover EA packaging command line that describes the archive layout from EA's own toolchain rather than by inference from bytes. It is a NON-PIXEL corroboration, and it is unrelated to the withdrawn decoded-pixel authenticity argument.
corroborates: that sg1/sg2 are group markers under a textures group
build_toolchain_artifact.does_not_establish: anything about install behaviour on a retail console, or that this tree is unmodified. It is a build artefact, not a shipped asset.

structural_variants.revision_1_claim: 'Two structural variants, one per platform generation.' That was scoped to the BIGF member shape alone and read as though it covered the whole format. Withdrawn as stated.

what_is_actually_uniform.gen7_member_shape: All 37 120 Gen7 archives accepted by the inspection parser carry exactly 6 members in the name pattern ['0', '<num>', 'sg1', '<num>', 'sg2', '1'], with exactly 1 texture payload each. Zero exceptions in either group.
what_is_actually_uniform.note: Member names were normalised: the two numeric member names are per-archive APT resource ids and vary. Not normalising them fragments the tuple into thousands of pseudo-variants, which is an artefact of the id and not a structural difference.

what_still_varies_and_is_a_real_variant: dimensions - three co-existing sizes on the Gen7 targets
mip count - base-level-only versus mip-chain headers, on the PS3 copy only
colour format - the PS4 num_format field is 0 on 10 246 files and 9 on 175
PS4 dst_sel_x - 7 on the majority, 0 on the same 175 files
structural_variants.distinct_observed_structural_tuples: 15 across the five folders (13 Gen7, 2 PS4), enumerated with exact counts in c0-por1-census.json. This is the honest variant count once dimensions, mips, colour format and group are included.

count_kinds.files_inventoried: every file present in the five folders, including backup-labelled files and the one .options artefact: 47 542
count_kinds.archives_or_texture_files_accepted: files accepted by the inspection parser: 47 541 (the .options file is the single exclusion)

path_and_id_observations.filename_conformance: all 37 120 Gen7 archives match p<digits>.big (or .big.bak); all 10 421 PS4 files match p<digits>.gnf; zero non-conforming names
path_and_id_observations.withdrawn_claim: Revision 1 stated that the id-to-bucket rule 'is NOT the literal folder-name ranges' and presented that as a finding. No candidate bucket function was ever formulated or tested, so only the membership above is known. That p8001_12000 contains ids above 12000 is an observation about membership, not an identified rule.
path_and_id_observations.identity_caveat: The numeric id is observed in the filename only. Its binding to any database field (ubPc.lOnr is used for this elsewhere in the application) was not examined.

cross_target_observation.what_was_run: For a seeded (seed=7) sample of 25 ids per folder from the p0_4000 bucket only, the PS3 and Xbox 360 DXT5 block streams were compared after undoing the Xbox 360 8-in-16 byte swap and 2D tiling. Full output in c0-por1-specimen-hashes.json.
cross_target_observation.result: 50 compared; 49 identical; 1 differing. The differing file, playerheadssmall/p127.big, is a PS3 current file that has a backup-labelled sibling; that sibling's block stream does match the Xbox 360 file.
cross_target_observation.what_this_establishes: That for these 50 specimens, the Xbox 360-specific stages produce the same block stream the PS3 file holds directly. Because the BIGF, RefPack and DXT5 stages are the SAME CODE on both sides, a fault common to both would cancel out and would not be detected.
what_this_does_NOT_establish: that the Xbox 360 tree is authentic, unmodified, or the set the game ships - revision 1 used it that way and that use is WITHDRAWN
that PS3 and Xbox 360 portraits are equivalent target-wide; this is 50 ids in one bucket of one title
any target-scoped format constraint on either platform

alpha_observation.scope: SPECIMEN OBSERVATION ONLY - three PS3 specimens: playerheads/p0_4000/p1008.big, playerheads/p0_4000/p1.big, playerheadssmall/p0_4000/p1008.big.
alpha_observation.method: Decoded with the C0-POR1 DXT5 decoder (por1_formats.decode_dxt5), then tested whether any colour channel exceeds alpha on semi-transparent texels.
alpha_observation.result: It does, by up to 253/255, which is inconsistent with premultiplied content on those specimens.
alpha_observation.withdrawn_claim: Revision 1 recorded target-wide 'straight' alpha. Three files decoded by one decoder do not support a target-wide constraint, and the profile's raster block no longer carries one.

ps4_header_observations.nature: All values below are INTERPRETATIONS of GNM T# descriptor bitfields, using the layout documented in crates/tdb-rx2/src/gnf.rs. No PS4 pixel data was decoded in this package.
ps4_header_observations.codec: data_format 41 (0x29) maps to BC7 in the GCN IMG_DATA_FORMAT table. That is a documented table lookup, not a decode.
ps4_header_observations.padding_arithmetic: 180480 - 256 = 180224 = 128 x 88 blocks x 16 bytes, which is consistent with a 512x352 padded surface carrying 340 logical rows.
withdrawn_claims: Revision 1 said the 384 all-zero blocks 'independently confirm' the 340 logical height. They are CONSISTENT with 3 padding block rows but have other explanations - a blank image region encodes identically - so they are not independent confirmation. The height is read from the descriptor.

Revision 1 argued the surface must be tiled because a linear surface would carry no padding. Linear surfaces can be pitch-padded, so the padding does not imply tiling. The only evidence for the tiling mode is the tiling_index field.

specimens.note: 22 named specimens with exact relative paths, byte sizes, SHA-256 digests and group labels, generated by por1_specimens.py. Digests are unchanged from revision 1; only the group labels were corrected.

coverage_limits: Container and texture headers were parsed for every file in the five folders, so the count and header-field distributions are census results rather than extrapolations. Pixel-level decoding was NOT: it covers a handful of PS3 and Xbox 360 specimens plus the 50-id block-stream comparison, and no PS4 file at all.
Only NHL Legacy (PS3, Xbox 360) and NHL 21 (PS4) were examined. Nothing transfers to any other title or platform.

The Xbox 360 and PS4 corpora are derived trees, so nothing here establishes shipping discovery, install or outer-archive packaging for those targets - and nothing measured on them is attributable to the shipped title.
The PS3 corpus is an observed installed copy carrying third-party writes, and patch.big was never opened.
Colour space was not measured on the Gen7 targets and is not uniform on PS4.

This package exercised code written for it, not this repository's parsers, with one exception (the transcribed Xbox 360 tiling formula). It is therefore NOT a qualification of tdb-rx2, tdb-archive-big or tdb-archive-codec.
No portrait was written, repacked, replaced or installed, and no support level or game-acceptance is claimed or implied by any entry in this file.
